about: MUTATING — creates an organisation's repository on GitHub, and nothing else (infra/forge/github-act.sh create-repository). Design 76155676 decision 4 (David 2026-09-27: GitHub acts are bounded verbs, plan then passkey-approved write, each proving by reading GitHub back; backlog 6a8ff89f): the rehearsal for a repository per hosting customer, first exercised on algedonic-dev/boss-dr, the private disaster-recovery copy of forge main. AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY in design 17835005's shape: it declares requires_approval with plan-a-github-repository as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders from GitHub and acts only while the bytes hash alike, which also makes a second run of an applied plan a refusal. Its bound is the script's: ONE create, POST /orgs/<owner>/repos with the name, the visibility and auto_init false, then ONE setting, PUT /repos/<owner>/<name>/actions/permissions {"enabled":false} (backlog e727fcfd, 2026-09-29: GitHub enables Actions on every new repository, and this verb's repositories are BOSS-managed copies whose workflows are the forge's — on the private DR copy each push of forge main would run the tree's workflows on paid minutes); both are named in the plan the passkey signs, and a repository that already stands as declared with Actions on plans the PUT alone — never a fork (no /forks call exists in the script, and a repository already standing as a fork is refused), never a visibility change, an archive or a delete. It authenticates as the GitHub App's INSTALLATION on <owner>, the request's first argument: the one-hour installation token the credential broker mints (credential.rotate.github-app-installation) and the forge converge renders into /etc/boss-publish/github-app/<owner>.token beside its recorded expiry — per-owner DATA, so a customer's organisation is a slot, never a constant. A slot that is absent, loose, not root's, empty or expired is a refusal before GitHub is called; the token travels only in a private header file and is never printed. Proof: GET /repos/<owner>/<name> reads back as <owner>/<name>, that visibility, fork false, and its Actions read back as enabled false — a 201 or a 204 that does not read back is exit 1. Any other 4xx or 5xx is exit 1 naming GitHub's words.
effect: ^github-act: proven — GET /repos/.+ reads back as .+, private .+, fork false; Actions read back as enabled false
